Saffron Biscotti

Served at: St. Lucia's Day

Makes about 24-30 biscottiPrep 25 minCook 50-60 min

Saffron Biscotti, with their beautiful golden hue, are a perfect treat to celebrate St. Lucia's Day, also known as Santa Lucia. The precious saffron spice symbolizes the light that St. Lucia brings during the darkest time of the year, offering a warm and comforting crunch alongside coffee or tea.

Ingredients

  • 1/4 teaspoon saffron threads
  • 2 tablespoons hot water or milk
  • 2 cups (240 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup (113 g) unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 cup (200 g) granulated sugar
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) slivered almonds (optional)

Method

  1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
  2. In a small bowl, steep the saffron threads in hot water or milk for 10 minutes to release their color and flavor.
  3. In a medium bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
  4. In a large bowl, cream together the softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
  5. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla extract and the saffron mixture.
  6. Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, mixing until just combined. Fold in the slivered almonds, if using. The dough will be stiff.
  7. Divide the dough in half. On the prepared baking sheet, shape each half into a log, approximately 10-12 inches (25-30 cm) long and 2 inches (5 cm) wide. Leave space between logs.
  8. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the logs are firm to the touch and lightly golden.
  9. Remove from the oven and let cool on the baking sheet for 10-15 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 300°F (150°C).
  10. Carefully transfer the logs to a cutting board. Using a serrated knife, slice each log diagonally into 1/2-inch (1.25 cm) thick pieces.
  11. Lay the sliced biscotti cut-side down back onto the baking sheet.
  12. Bake for another 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the biscotti are golden brown and crisp.
  13. Transfer the biscotti to a wire rack to cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

Tips

  • For an extra festive touch, you can drizzle cooled biscotti with melted white chocolate.
  • Ensure the saffron steeps long enough to maximize its flavor and color.
  • Biscotti are meant to be hard; they are traditionally dipped in coffee, tea, or dessert wine.
